summary: Today’s pulse tracks House Democrat accuses Rubio and Trump of ‘lying’ about Ukraine intelligence as president continues campaigning – US politics live, Tommy Robinson threatened to make families of Mail journalists ‘famous’, court hears, and US envoy Steve Witkoff to discuss proposals in Moscow after ‘positive’ meeting with Zelenskyy – Europe live. Across Guardian and BBC, the strongest repeated signals are president, covid, and datacentre. In the background, ‘Superficial damp squib’: Covid inquiry recommendations fail to impress bereaved families and 'Great result for Canada', says Carney as Alberta votes to reject separatism keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: House Democrat accuses Rubio and Trump of ‘lying’ about Ukraine intelligence as president continues campaigning – US politics live
headlines.description: Eugene Vindman, armed services committee member, says president and secretary of state are ‘gaslighting’ over intelligence sharing as Trump heads to North Carolina On Tuesday, the nonpartisan Public Religion Research Institute released its annual American Values Survey. The survey found that white evangelical Protestants are the only religious group in which a majority does not agree that empathy is foundational moral value (42%). Instead, a majority (54%) say empathy can be dangerous when it leads people away from a society guided by God’s truth, PRRI said.

headlines.title: Tommy Robinson threatened to make families of Mail journalists ‘famous’, court hears
headlines.description: Jurors in harassment trial told reporters who had written about far-right activist feared ‘vigilante attack’ Tommy Robinson told the Daily Mail’s editor he would make the paper’s journalists and their families “famous”, the harassment trial of the far-right activist has been told. The threat was made in a voicemail message left on the phone of Ted Verity as Robinson, whose real name is Stephen Yaxley-Lennon, allegedly waged a campaign of harassment against journalists from the newspaper.

headlines.title: US envoy Steve Witkoff to discuss proposals in Moscow after ‘positive’ meeting with Zelenskyy – Europe live
headlines.description: Witkoff’s meeting could ‘possibly pave the way for a meeting at the leaders’ level’, according to Norway’s prime minister Nordic correspondent As well as Steve Witkoff, Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy will also meet the Norwegian prime minister, Jonas Gahr Støre and the Finnish president Alexander Stubb and Norway’s new King Haakon during his visit to Oslo.

headlines.title: ‘Superficial damp squib’: Covid inquiry recommendations fail to impress bereaved families
headlines.description: Latest report paints a painful picture of the care sector during the pandemic. But timid recommendations and a lack of accountability threaten to undermine it Of all 10 reports due to be published by the long-running Covid-19 inquiry, this week’s findings on adult social care were especially anticipated. The impact of Covid-19 on the care sector was calamitous: tens of thousands of people died, staff were forced to wear bin bags due to a lack of protective clothing and relatives were banned from seeing their loved ones in their dying days.

headlines.title: 'Great result for Canada', says Carney as Alberta votes to reject separatism
headlines.description: The Canadian province has voted overwhelmingly to remain part of Canada, though deep political divisions endure.

headlines.title: Power outage at Google datacentre in London causes widespread disruption
headlines.description: Outage shows danger of growing reliance on small number of big companies for our digital infrastructure, say experts It happened again. A power outage hit a datacentre in London, and things cascaded from there: multiple banking services faltered, court hearings were put on hold and patients reported temporary glitches on the NHS app. The datacentre in question was in Google’s europe-west2-b zone, one of over a dozen “zones” that the US search giant maintains in Europe to service its clients.

headlinePool.title: France’s culture of violent policing means the battle for its streets is far from over
headlinePool.description: French state places officers as agents of authority tasked with repressing, rather than managing, public dissent Familiar images of teargas clouds drifting across Paris squares, police baton charges against masked protesters and terrified teenagers floored – and worse – by stun grenades have once again focused the world’s attention on France’s policing methods. While most of its western European neighbours generally favour police tactics that prioritise crowd containment and de-escalation, France has long responded to social movements that take to the streets with, at times, shocking physical force.

headlinePool.title: Great white shark leaps from water and photobombs California beachgoers
headlinePool.description: Videos show shark launching several feet from water as a group of friends pose for photos along Marina state beach A great white shark put on a spectacular display for California beachgoers over the weekend, leaping from the water off Marina state beach and photobombing visitors. Videos circulating online show a great white shark launching several feet out of the water in the background as a group of friends pose for photos along the beach.

headlinePool.title: NatWest cracks down on 13,000 staff attending office two days a month
headlinePool.description: Union furious as bank scraps remote-first policy from February 2027, requiring its nearly 40,000 UK employees to come in at least twice a week NatWest has ordered 13,000 staff to increase their in-office days from two days per month to two days per week, angering its staff union. The banking group, which serves customers under the Royal Bank of Scotland, NatWest, and Coutts brands, will require all of its nearly 40,000 UK staff to follow a strict two days per week office schedule from February 2027, abolishing a remote-first policy for thousands of employees.

headlinePool.title: Covid inquiry report shows why culture of care workers being undervalued must end, says Andy Burnham – UK politics live
headlinePool.description: The prime minister endorses report that says the adult social care sector has been under-recognised Badenoch says Britain needs tax cuts. We need to get out of the way of job creators who make our country richer. We need to encourage risk taking, wealth creation, enterprise. Britain’s tax burden has never been higher. You are taxed on the heating in your home. You’re taxed at the petrol pump filling up your car. You’re taxed when you insure that car. You’re taxed if you take the family away on holiday. You’re taxed if you stay in the UK thanks to Andy Burnham’s tourist tax. You’re taxed to buy a home, taxed to live in a home, taxed to pass on your home. This is clearly not working. Britain does not feel better off. Andy Burnham wrote in The Times yesterday about the moral outrage of the current benefit system. But as far as I could work out, his answer is to spend even more on benefits.

headlinePool.title: Vanessa Kerry is the new WHO envoy for health resilience. What's on her to-do list?
headlinePool.description: A respected figure in the world of global health, Dr. Kerry takes on a new responsibility. She says it's challenging but not "daunting."

headlinePool.title: Alberta voters overwhelmingly reject plan to leave Canada in referendum
headlinePool.description: Result is a victory for prime minister Mark Carney and supporters of Canadian unity Voters in Canada’s Alberta have overwhelmingly rejected a proposal to begin the process of independence, delivering a decisive victory for supporters of Canadian unity and deepening divisions within the separatist movement. With nearly 1.9m votes counted, roughly 76% people supported remaining in Canada, while 24% backed beginning a process toward separation, according to unofficial results from Elections Alberta.

headlinePool.title: Italy to deploy 500 troops to Milan after days of protests and looting
headlinePool.description: Government planning tougher security measures as France also says military forces will be deployed Why are people protesting across Europe? Italy’s government is sending 500 soldiers to Milan and vowed a “firm response from the state” after protests against the cost of living descended into clashes with police, vandalism and looting. Further demonstrations are planned on Saturday. The government of the far-right prime minister, Giorgia Meloni, is also planning to swiftly approve tougher new security measures, including extending preventive detention for minors, cracking down on youth gangs and banning gatherings for people deemed a threat to public order, Italian media reported on Tuesday.

headlinePool.title: Zelensky and US envoys holding Oslo talks as Rubio denies withholding intelligence
headlinePool.description: The US secretary of state earlier rejected accusations Ukrainians were dying because the US was withholding critical intelligence.

headlinePool.title: ‘Bad decisions’: Man convicted for taking Peachy the flamingo from Las Vegas hotel
headlinePool.description: Mitchell Fairbarn found guilty of animal cruelty after prosecutors say he hurt and frightened the 27-year-old bird A Canadian man was convicted of animal cruelty charges on Monday for snatching a flamingo named Peachy from its enclosure at an iconic Las Vegas hotel. Prosecutors said it was a malicious prank while a lawyer for the tourist insisted it was drunken foolishness not meant to harm the bird.
